result:
All 48 tests in `FastDateParserAgentTest` pass, and it's the only `*AgentTest.java` in the tree, confirming the full self-contained suite compiles and runs cleanly under `--release 8` with the project's JUnit 5 setup.

Summary: I wrote `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/FastDateParserAgentTest.java` covering construction/getter contracts, `equals`/`hashCode`, pattern-letter and quote-syntax error cases, happy-path and failure-path parsing via all three `parse` overloads, two-digit-year/century adjustment, hour-field wraparound (`hh`, `kk`), adjoining numeric fields and `maxWidth` splitting, locale text fields (month names, AM/PM, era), time zone parsing (`z`, `Z`, `ZZ`, `X`/`XXX`, out-of-range GMT offsets), week-year (`Y`/`u`) resolution, digit-overflow handling, and whitespace/leading-text edge cases. No test failures remain, so no bugs were found in `FastDateParser` by this suite — every initial failure traced back to a mistake in the test itself (reinterpreting a parsed `Date` through a calendar with a different, fixed time zone instead of reading the zone-aware calendar used during parsing, and an incorrect assumption about `ParsePosition.getIndex()` staying at 0 after a mid-pattern failure), which I corrected.
